condition: subacute symmetric burning pain and pins-and-needles across the soles of both feet every night for 8 weeks in a Black man taking daily metformin
level_rationale: Eight weeks of nightly burning pain and pins and needles across the soles of both feet in a 66-year-old Black man taking daily metformin indicates subacute distal symmetric plantar sensory neuropathy or metformin-associated vitamin B12 deficiency warranting a routine outpatient physician visit for monofilament foot examination, glycemic and B12 testing, and neuropathic symptom management rather than emergency care, whereas the sole of the right foot turning ice cold and dusky slate gray today signals acute limb-threatening plantar arterial ischemia on dark skin requiring immediate emergency department vascular evaluation.
